biography.plain_text: Jerry Lee Wordsworth is an American food-distribution executive from Rocky Mount, North Carolina. He and his siblings bought their father's Meadowbrook Meat Company and transformed the local pork processor into MBM, a nationwide supplier to restaurant chains. As chairman and chief executive, he led the family company until its sale to McLane.

long_biography.plain_text:
MBM's shift from local meat processing to customised foodservice distribution defined Jerry Lee Wordsworth's leadership. The company replaced a retail-grocery model with supply programmes for national restaurant chains, built a network of distribution centres and combined food delivery with freight operations. Wordsworth served as chairman and chief executive as the Rocky Mount business grew across the United States.

Professional football added a separate public role. Wordsworth and his brother Steve held substantial minority interests in the Carolina Panthers for many years, remaining limited partners until the franchise's 2018 sale. He also supported professional education in North Carolina, making major unrestricted gifts to NC State's College of Veterinary Medicine and the University of North Carolina School of Law.
